title: A week in Cornwall without clubs

copy.heading: A week in Cornwall without clubs

blocks.text: This year the family went to Cornwall. The clubs were not packed. This was agreed in advance, in writing.

On the first day Dave walked on the beach and said the sand was "very fine", which the family understood was a comment on bunkers. On the second day he went to the shop for milk and came back two hours later having "had a look" at a course on the cliff. He did not play. He watched a four-ball putt out on the 18th and stood at the fence making small noises. On the third day he hired a putter for the crazy golf and lost to his son, who is six.
By the end of the week Dave had swum in the sea twice, eaten a pasty on the harbour wall, and been in all but one of the family photographs. The Programme records the week as a partial success.

blocks.label: Case notes (Sue), Day 38
blocks.text: Crazy golf. He lost to Alfie on the windmill hole and asked for a rematch. Alfie said no. Best thing I've seen all year.
